faqs.q: What is a Destaco 2P series 2-jaw precision parallel gripper used for?
faqs.a: A Destaco 2P series 2-jaw precision parallel gripper is a pneumatic gripper whose two jaws move in a straight line toward or away from each other to hold a part during automated handling. This listing carries 8 part numbers, from 8002P to 16502P, with cylinder bores of 2.36", 2.99" and 4.72". Other jaw styles are on our [grippers and rotary actuators shelf](/c/pneumatic-grippers-actuators).

faqs.q: How do you read a Destaco 2P part number such as 11002P-P-RE-C-E3-V?
faqs.a: The digits before 2P give the gripper size and 2P marks the 2-jaw version, so 11002P is the size with the 2.99" bore. The letters that follow are factory options; on this listing 11002P-P-RE-C-E3-V is the long-stroke 1.18" version. Quote the full part number so the options are supplied exactly.

faqs.q: What bore and stroke sizes does the Destaco 2P precision gripper come in?
faqs.a: This listing covers three bores: 2.36" (8002P, 0.51" stroke, 3.15" maximum finger length), 2.99" (11002P, 1.18" stroke, 4.13" fingers) and 4.72" (16502P, 1.18" stroke, 4.53" fingers). Smaller and larger bores, plus long-stroke versions, are on the [Destaco 2P Series Parallel Grippers listing](/p/destaco-2p-series-parallel-grippers).

faqs.q: How do I choose between the 8002P, 11002P and 16502P precision grippers?
faqs.a: Pick the 2P size whose grip force at your supply pressure covers the part weight times its acceleration with a safety margin, and whose finger length limit covers your tooling. The 8002P suits fingers up to 3.15", the 11002P up to 4.13" and the 16502P up to 4.53". Our gripper sizing guide explains the force calculation.

faqs.q: What air pressure does a Destaco 2P precision parallel gripper need?
faqs.a: The Destaco 2P series runs on 30 to 100 psi compressed air (about 2.1 to 6.9 bar), and 30 psi is the minimum shown for every sized row on this listing. Grip force rises with pressure, so size the gripper at the lowest pressure your plant can guarantee rather than the nominal line pressure.

faqs.q: Which medium does a Destaco 2P series gripper run on?
faqs.a: The Destaco 2P precision gripper is pneumatic and runs on clean, dry compressed air within the 30 to 100 psi range. Fit a filter and regulator upstream so water and dirt do not reach the piston seals; matching units are on our filters, regulators and lubricators shelf.

faqs.q: Which standards or certificates come with Destaco 2P precision parallel grippers?
faqs.a: Destaco does not state a product standard for the 2P precision gripper on this listing, and we hold no certificate documents for it. If your project needs a certificate of conformity or the maker's datasheet, say so in the enquiry and we request it from Destaco with the order.

faqs.q: What do you need to fit a Destaco 2P gripper to a machine?
faqs.a: A 2P gripper needs custom fingers machined to your part, a valve to switch the two air ports, and tubing and fittings to suit. Directional valves are on our solenoid valves shelf, and push-in fittings and silencers on the fittings shelf.

faqs.q: How should Destaco 2P precision grippers be installed and maintained?
faqs.a: Mount the 2P gripper on a flat surface, keep the fingers within the maker's finger length limit for the size and set the air pressure at the regulator, not by restricting flow. Check periodically for air leaks, jaw play and finger wear, and quote the full part number when ordering a replacement.

faqs.q: What is the difference between the Destaco 2P and 3P precision grippers?
faqs.a: The 2P has two jaws and suits flat-sided or prismatic parts, while the [Destaco 3P 3-jaw gripper](/p/destaco-3p-series-3-jaw-parallel-grippers) centres round parts such as shafts and discs on three jaws. Both ranges use the same size numbering in front of 2P or 3P, so matching sizes share a bore.

faqs.q: What are Destaco 2P series parallel grippers used for?

faqs.q: What does the -C suffix mean on a Destaco 2P gripper such as 8002P-P-C?
faqs.a: On this listing the -C rows are the long-stroke versions of each 2P size: 8002P-P has a 0.51" stroke and 8002P-P-C 0.79", 6002P-P 0.39" and 6002P-P-C 0.63". Other letters, such as RE, RI, SD and V, select factory options; quote the full part number and we confirm them before supply.

faqs.q: Which bore sizes does the Destaco 2P parallel gripper range cover?
faqs.a: The 2P range on this listing covers five bores: 1.57" (6002P), 2.36" (8002P), 2.99" (11002P), 4.13" (14002P) and 4.72" (16502P). A bigger bore gives more grip force at the same air pressure, so choose the bore from the force you need, then the stroke.

faqs.q: What jaw strokes are available on Destaco 2P parallel grippers?
faqs.a: Destaco 2P strokes on this listing run from 0.39" (10 mm) on the 6002P to 1.97" (50 mm) on the long-stroke 16502P-P-C. The 14002P comes in 1.02" (26 mm) and 1.57" (40 mm); pick a stroke that clears the part plus its position tolerance. Our [gripper guide](/blog/pneumatic-grippers-and-vacuum-guide) covers stroke and force sizing.

faqs.q: What operating pressure range do Destaco 2P parallel grippers have?
faqs.a: Destaco 2P parallel grippers operate on 30 to 100 psi compressed air, about 2.1 to 6.9 bar, as listed for the 8002P and 16502P sizes. Grip force depends on the pressure actually at the gripper, so check it after the valve and tubing, not only at the compressor.

faqs.q: What air quality do Destaco 2P grippers need?
faqs.a: Destaco 2P grippers need clean, dry compressed air with a filter and regulator ahead of the valve. Water and particles wear the piston seals and slow the jaws; our [ISO 8573-1 air quality guide](/blog/compressed-air-quality-iso-8573-1) explains which purity class to aim for.

faqs.q: How are Destaco 2P series grippers maintained?

faqs.q: What is the difference between the 8002P and 14002P Destaco grippers?

faqs.q: What finger length can a Destaco 3P 3-jaw gripper take?

faqs.q: What air pressure does a Destaco 3P 3-jaw gripper run at?

faqs.q: What cup styles and sizes are in the Destaco ARV vacuum cup range?

faqs.q: How do I choose between flat and bellows Destaco vacuum cups?
faqs.a: Use a flat cup such as VC-F30N-18M on flat, rigid surfaces for the best holding stiffness, and a micro-bellows or multi-bellows cup where the part is curved, uneven or at varying height. Our [grippers and vacuum guide](/blog/pneumatic-grippers-and-vacuum-guide) explains pad sizing.

faqs.a: Maximum finger length is 3 1/2" on the DPDS-088M-025, 4" on the DPDS-125M-038-B and 8" on the DPDS-250M-075. Stay within the limit, as longer fingers overload the jaw guides.

faqs.q: What is the accuracy of a Destaco DPDS parallel gripper?
faqs.a: Destaco lists an accuracy of -0.002" to +0.002" for the DPDS-088M-025 and -0.003" to +0.003" for the DPDS-125M-038-B and DPDS-250M-075. The DPDS runs from 20 psi upward on compressed air.

faqs.q: What air supply does a Destaco DPDS parallel gripper need?
faqs.a: A Destaco DPDS needs clean, dry, regulated compressed air from 20 psi, with a filter and regulator ahead of the valve so water and dirt do not reach the seals. Filter-regulators are on our [FRL shelf](/c/air-preparation-frl).

faqs.q: How do you maintain a Destaco DPDS parallel gripper?

faqs.q: What is a Destaco DPE series electric parallel gripper used for?
faqs.a: A Destaco DPE series gripper is an electric 2-jaw parallel gripper that grips parts without compressed air, for robots and machines where air is unavailable or unwanted. This listing carries 10 part numbers in the DPE-400-10 and DPE-400-20 sizes.

faqs.q: How do you read a Destaco DPE part number such as DPE-400-10-ID-P?
faqs.a: DPE-400 is the gripper body and 10 or 20 the stroke version; ID or OD follows, and the last letter gives the sensor output, P for PNP or N for NPN. DPE-400-10 and DPE-400-20 without endings are the base versions.

faqs.q: What stroke and grip force does the Destaco DPE electric gripper have?
faqs.a: The DPE-400-10 has a 0.39" stroke and 300 lbf grip force, and the DPE-400-20 a 0.78" stroke and 200 lbf. Choose the shorter stroke for more force, the longer one where the jaws must open wider.

faqs.q: How big is the Destaco DPE-400 electric parallel gripper?
faqs.a: The DPE-400 is listed at 4.9 inch size on the ID and OD versions, for both the 10 and 20 strokes. Check the maker's drawing for mounting and cable exit before designing the tooling.

faqs.q: What protection class does the Destaco DPE electric gripper have?
faqs.a: Destaco rates the DPE electric parallel gripper IP50, which under IEC 60529 means dust-protected with no stated protection against water. Keep it out of coolant spray and wash-down; for wet areas a pneumatic gripper such as the [Destaco DPDL](/p/destaco-dpdl-series-general-purpose-parallel-grippers-modular) may suit better.

faqs.q: Which sensor outputs are available on Destaco DPE grippers?
faqs.a: Destaco offers the DPE with an optional PNP or NPN sensor, coded -P or -N at the end of the part number, for example DPE-400-20-OD-P or DPE-400-20-OD-N. Match the output to the inputs on your PLC or robot controller.

faqs.q: What certificates come with Destaco DPE electric grippers?

faqs.q: Which cables and accessories does Destaco list for the DPE gripper?
faqs.a: Destaco lists OISA-004, OISA-005, CABL-013, CABL-052 and CABL-053 as accessories for the DPE, covering sensors and cables. The DPE is direct connect; ask us to confirm the cable for your controller.

faqs.q: How do you maintain a Destaco DPE electric gripper?
faqs.a: Keep the DPE clean and dry within its IP50 rating, check the jaws for play and the fingers for wear, and inspect the cable for damage. There are no air seals to service, but replace a worn unit with the same part number.

faqs.q: Should I choose a Destaco electric DPE or a pneumatic parallel gripper?
faqs.a: Choose the DPE where compressed air is not available, and a pneumatic gripper such as the [Destaco DPDS](/p/destaco-dpds-series-compact-robust-parallel-grippers) where air is on hand and cycle cost matters. The DPE-400-10 gives 300 lbf with synchronous jaws.
